$comment: One defect per fixture. Each fixture has a defective app.html and a correct.html twin, which is what makes attribution unambiguous: a suite that fails on the defective variant and passes on the correct one has caught that defect and nothing else.

fixtures.title: Password field has no label
fixtures.description: The password control is a bare placeholder with no <label for>, so it has no accessible name.
fixtures.whyItMatters: Screen reader users are told only 'edit text'. A core login control is unusable without sight.

fixtures.title: Clickable div used as a radio control
fixtures.description: Payment method is a pair of divs with onclick. No role, not focusable, no keyboard operation.
fixtures.whyItMatters: The control cannot be operated by keyboard at all, and assistive technology does not announce it as a control.

fixtures.title: Empty submit produces no feedback
fixtures.description: Submitting the login form with empty fields does nothing: no message, no alert, no focus move.
fixtures.whyItMatters: The user cannot tell whether the form was ignored, failed, or is still submitting.

fixtures.title: Reflected XSS via innerHTML
fixtures.description: The search query is written into the DOM with innerHTML and no escaping, so a crafted query executes script.
fixtures.whyItMatters: Arbitrary script execution in the user's session. Highest severity in the corpus.

fixtures.title: Declared age range is not enforced
fixtures.description: min=18 and max=120 are present in the markup, but nothing checks them in code, so an age of 5 is accepted silently.
fixtures.whyItMatters: A declared constraint that is not enforced is worse than no constraint: it looks handled.
